svg.title: One line of prose on stdout against the same diagnostic on stderr
svg.desc: Two panels. On the left, marked with a cross, a tool calls print then returns: standard output carries the bare word connected, flagged as not JSON, followed by a valid JSON-RPC frame, and the client parser below reports failing to parse the message with an invalid JSON error at line 1 column 1. A note says the connection breaks at that byte rather than at your tool. On the right, marked with a tick, the same tool logs instead of printing: standard output carries only the frame and reaches the client parser, while standard error carries the word connected to the host log on a separate arrow. Notes say the frame stream stays valid, that a client may capture, forward or ignore standard error, and that it should not read output there as a sign of failure. A closing line warns that the bug is intermittent because standard output is block-buffered when it is a pipe.
svg.text: A stray line on stdout stops the frame stream from being JSON
The rule is one line long: the server must not write anything to stdout that is not a valid MCP message.
The same pipe the protocol uses.
Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
The connection breaks at that byte, not at your tool.
The frame stream stays valid, and your diagnostics still reach you.
A client may capture, forward, or ignore stderr, and should not
read it as a sign of failure.
It is intermittent: stdout is block-buffered when it is a pipe, so a short print may not fail on the run that introduced it.
